pages.title: Projects
pages.content:
00 · Work

Projects

Kosei Architects shows four finished buildings on this page: an office, a housing court, a renovated mill, and a school annex.

00

Four finished buildings

Harbour Workshops in Ostend is the office, in use since 2023, with 180 desks in 4,200 m² of a 1960s warehouse. Linden Court in Leuven is co-housing from 2022, with 24 apartments, a shared garden, a timber frame, and deck access. Old Mill studios in Ghent is the renovation, a flour mill turned in 2024 into 14 workshops across 1,600 m². Rivière school annex in Namur is a timber annex of 6 classrooms and 900 m², built in 11 months and completed in 2021. The same four appear as a wall of photographs and again as a list.

Nothing on this page is a prize, a press clipping, or a promise about the next job. Each project stays tied to the question it answered and to the rooms now in use. Filter the list with the text links All, Workplaces, Housing, and Renovation. The school annex remains visible under All.

Filter All · Workplaces · Housing · Renovation

Title

Explanation

01 · Workplaces · 2023

Harbour Workshops, Ostend

Harbour Workshops is filed under Workplaces. A logistics firm needed one floor for 180 desks inside a 1960s warehouse in Ostend.

The work added a timber mezzanine and roof lights and kept the steel frame. The office has been in use since 2023. The floor area is 4,200 m², and daylight reaches every desk. The building is also the subject of the timber model at 1:50 that sits on the studio table in Brussels. Question, work, and result are written out in full on the project page. On this list the row carries the place, the year, the type, and the area, then the short account of desks, mezzanine, and frame. It is the workplace we use when a client asks what an older structure can still hold.

↗

02 · Housing · 2022

Linden Court housing, Leuven

Linden Court is filed under Housing. It is co-housing in Leuven, completed in 2022: 24 apartments, a shared garden, a timber frame, and deck access.

The shared yard sits between the housing blocks, with benches and bicycles in the court. The building and the yard are one project, not two addresses. We publish them together so the apartments are not read as a stack of private rooms alone. Deck access and the shared garden are part of how the court is used day to day. Linden Court is the housing project we point to for both co-housing and a small apartment building. Figures stay as they are: 24 apartments, 2022, Leuven. We do not add a second housing scheme on this list.

↗

03 · Renovation · 2024

Old Mill studios, Ghent

Old Mill studios is filed under Renovation. In Ghent a flour mill became 14 workshops, completed in 2024, with a floor area of 1,600 m².

The renovated hall is brick, with white steel and daylight in the workshops. Before, the building was a mill. After, it is a set of rooms where people work. The row in the list gives the year, the area, and the count of workshops, then points to the renovation page for the longer before-and-after account. We do not treat the mill as a new workplace built on an empty site. The point of the project is the reuse itself. Fourteen workshops is the result we state, not a target for every industrial building that follows.

↗

04 · School · 2021

Rivière school annex, Namur

Rivière school annex sits on the full list under All. It is a timber annex in Namur, completed in 2021, with 6 classrooms and 900 m², built in 11 months.

It is not an office floor and it is not housing. It is a school building, and we leave it described that way. The list row gives the place, the year, the number of classrooms, the area, and the eleven months of building. There is no separate renovation story and no desk count. When the list is filtered to Workplaces, Housing, or Renovation, this annex is not forced into those three labels. It remains part of the wall and of the unfiltered list, as one of the four finished buildings the studio publishes.

↗

First meeting

A first meeting is free: 60 minutes at the studio or on site, and a written note of the brief.

pages.title: Harbour Workshops
pages.content:
00 · Workplaces · Ostend · 2023

Harbour Workshops

A logistics firm needed one floor for 180 desks in a 1960s warehouse in Ostend.

01

Question

A logistics firm needed one floor for 180 desks in a 1960s warehouse in Ostend. That was the question, and it was a use question before it was a look question. The warehouse was already there. The steel frame was already there. The firm did not ask for a new office building on an empty plot. It asked how one floor could hold 180 desks and still be a place people could work.

Kosei Architects took that sentence as the brief. We did not rename the client, and we do not add a headcount, a shift pattern, or a second floor to the story. The published area of the project is 4,200 m². The year the office came into use is 2023. Everything drawn after the first meeting had to answer that one demand: desks in the warehouse, in daylight, without discarding the frame.

02

Work

The work was a timber mezzanine, roof lights, and a decision to keep the steel frame. New timber was set into the warehouse rather than used to replace it. Roof lights were added so the floor would not depend on the outer wall alone for daylight. The mezzanine is the piece that makes a working floor inside the older volume. During design the building was studied as a timber model at 1:50, a three-storey office model on the studio table, with tracing paper and a steel ruler beside it.

Sketch stages on our jobs also include a model at 1:100, with plans, sections, and a cost estimate. The Harbour model that we show is the one at 1:50. Consultants were coordinated where the permit set required it. The construction stage then followed the contract, with the frame left in place.

03

Result

Harbour Workshops has been in use since 2023. There are 180 desks, and daylight reaches every desk. The result is the same number the question asked for, in the warehouse that was already standing, with the steel frame kept. We state that as the outcome of this project. We do not turn it into a promise that every later office will have the same desk count, the same daylight, or the same programme.

The building is an office of 4,200 m² in Ostend. People use it on working days. The timber model remains in the studio as the record of how the floor was studied before it was built. If you want the fee side of a workplace job, the figures sit on the fees page, starting from the free first meeting and running through full service at 9 % of the build cost.

04

Facts

The facts below are the ones we are willing to print: no award, no product brand, no energy figure.

Result: in use since 2023, 180 desks, daylight at every desk. Model: timber, 1:50, of this office. Studio: Kosei Architects, Quai des Charbonnages 12, 1080 Brussels, Belgium. The practice was founded in 2008 and has eight people. These are the facts we are willing to print. There is no award attached to the project, no named product brand, and no energy figure is stated. The next office we draw will have its own brief, its own site, and its own cost. Harbour Workshops is one finished answer, recorded so a new client can see the order we work in: question, then work, then result.

Place

Ostend, Belgium

Year

2023

Type

Office

Area

4,200 m²

Desks

180

Work

Timber mezzanine, roof lights, steel frame kept

05

Photographs

Three photographs carry this project. The first is the office interior: the timber mezzanine, the roof lights, and the desks on the working floor. The second is the warehouse itself, the steel frame that stayed, with the new timber set into it. The third is the model on the studio table, captioned Timber model, 1:50 · Harbour Workshops, Ostend. It shows a three-storey office building in light timber, at eye level, on a pale table against a white wall. We do not publish a night view, a drone view, or a portrait of the logistics firm.

The three pictures match the three lines of the story. The model is how the floor was studied. The frame is what was kept. The interior is the floor in use, with daylight at the desks. Captions stay short on purpose. The numbers live in the facts, not in a corner of the photograph.

A first meeting is free: 60 minutes at the studio or on site, and a written note of the brief.

pages.title: Workplaces
pages.content:
01 · Work

Workplaces

A workplace project at Kosei Architects starts with a question about use, not with a style.

00 Approach

01 Projects

02 Fees

03 Questions

00

Approach

Who has to sit here, what is already standing, and where does daylight need to land. We draw slowly so the building can be used for a long time. Every project starts with a question, not a style. For offices, the clearest finished example is Harbour Workshops in Ostend. A logistics firm needed one floor for 180 desks in a 1960s warehouse.

The answer was a timber mezzanine and roof lights, with the steel frame kept. The office has been in use since 2023, at 4,200 m², with daylight at every desk. Workplaces on this page also include rooms that are not desk-farms: workshops in a former mill, and a school annex where people teach. Interior fit-out, when the shell exists, is a separate service at €38 per m². We do not promise a headcount, a permit, or a construction price.

Title

Explanation

01 · Ostend · 2023

Harbour Workshops, Ostend

Harbour Workshops is the office on our list. Ostend, 2023, 4,200 m², inside a 1960s warehouse.

The question was one floor for 180 desks for a logistics firm. The work was a timber mezzanine, roof lights, and the existing steel frame kept. The result is the floor in use since 2023, 180 desks, daylight at every desk. The timber model at 1:50 in the studio is this building, shown as a three-storey office on the table. We use the project when a client has an older frame and a present-day floor of work. We do not treat 180 desks as a standard. It is the number this brief asked for. The full question, work, and result sit on the project page. Samuel Okafor is the project architect for workplaces and has been at the studio since 2016. The page does not claim he was the only author of this building.

↗

02 · Ghent · 2024

Old Mill studios, Ghent

Old Mill studios is a workplace made by renovation. In Ghent a flour mill was turned into 14 workshops, completed in 2024, across 1,600 m².

People work in those rooms. That is why the project sits on this page as well as on the renovation page. The renovated hall is brick, with white steel and daylight. Before, the building milled flour. After, it holds 14 workshops. We do not call it an office, and we do not give it a desk count. The workplace here is the workshop. The row is the second workplace project we publish, after Harbour Workshops and before the school annex. If your question is about keeping an industrial shell and putting work back inside it, read the renovation account for the before and after, then use this row for the simple fact: fourteen rooms for work, in a mill that was already there.

↗

03 · Namur · 2021

Rivière school annex, Namur

Rivière school annex in Namur is the third project row. It is a timber annex, completed in 2021, with 6 classrooms and 900 m², built in 11 months.

A classroom is a workplace for teaching, and we list the annex here as a building people use on working days, not as an office and not as housing. The structure is timber. The programme is six rooms for a school. Eleven months is the time this annex took to build. It is not a studio-wide construction period. Construction on other jobs runs per the contract. We do not invent a second school, a pupil count, or a teaching method. The row exists so workplace work is not reduced to a single open plan in Ostend. Offices, workshops, and this school annex are three different kinds of daily use. The fees below cover how such work is commissioned, not a special school tariff.

↗

02

Fees for workplace work

Workplace fees use the same list as the rest of the practice, in euro, excluding VAT. The first meeting is free: 60 minutes at the studio or on site, with a written note of the brief. A feasibility study is €3,800 and includes a site and planning check, two massing options, an area schedule, and a cost range. Sketch design is from €9,500 and includes plans, sections, a model at 1:100, and a cost estimate. Permit drawings are from €14,000 and include the full permit set, consultants coordinated, and submission.

Full service, design to handover, is 9 % of the build cost and includes all stages, site meetings, and a handover file. Interior workplace fit-out is €38 per m² and includes layout, finishes, and a furniture plan. Where the fee says from, that figure is a start, not a cap. We do not promise the build cost or a permit.

03

Questions

What do you need from a client before drawing a workplace?

We need the question the floor has to answer, and we need access to the site. At the first meeting, 60 minutes at Quai des Charbonnages 12 or on the site, we write a note of the brief. That meeting is free and by appointment. The brief and site visit stage that follows takes 2 weeks. If you already have drawings of the existing building, bring them. If you do not, we start from the visit. Harbour Workshops began as a sentence about 180 desks in a warehouse, not as a style board. A logistics firm could point to a real floor. You should be able to say who will use the rooms and what must stay. You do not need a finished brief, a brand book, or a construction price. Those come later, if at all. Feasibility, when you want it, is a separate study at €3,800. We will not invent a requirement you do not have.

What does a workplace commission cost?

It depends which line you hire, and every figure excludes VAT. A first meeting is free. Feasibility is €3,800. Sketch design starts from €9,500. Permit drawings start from €14,000. Full service, from design to handover, is 9 % of the build cost, not a fixed sum. If the build cost rises, that fee rises with it. If the build cost falls, the fee falls with it. We do not publish a sample construction price, and we do not lock one in advance. Interior workplace fit-out is €38 per m² for layout, finishes, and a furniture plan. A cost range is part of feasibility. A cost estimate is part of sketch design. Neither is a tender result. The word from on sketch design and permit drawings means the fee starts at that figure. It is not a statement that every office stays there. The same list is printed in full on the fees page.

How long does a workplace project take?

Four stages, and only the first three have a published span. Brief and site visit takes 2 weeks. Sketch design takes 6 to 8 weeks. Permit drawings take 10 to 12 weeks. The construction stage runs per the contract. We do not add those spans into a single total, because the contract stage has no fixed number of weeks, and a permit authority sits outside our calendar. The school annex in Namur was built in 11 months. That figure belongs to that timber annex alone. It is not the length of Harbour Workshops, and it is not a timetable we attach to the next office. The first meeting inside the opening stage is 60 minutes. The 2 weeks cover the brief and the site visit, not only that hour. Full service includes site meetings during construction and a handover file at the end. We do not name a start date or a completion date in advance.

First meeting

A first meeting is free: 60 minutes at the studio or on site, and a written note of the brief.

pages.title: Housing
pages.content:
02 · Work

Housing

Housing at Kosei Architects covers co-housing and small apartment buildings.

00 Co-housing

01 Small apartment buildings

02 Linden Court

00

Co-housing

The project we publish is Linden Court in Leuven, completed in 2022. It is co-housing of 24 apartments, with a shared garden, a timber frame, and deck access. The shared court is part of the housing, not a leftover space beside it. Between the blocks there is a courtyard garden, with benches and bicycles. People share the garden and reach their homes along the decks. That is the co-housing row.

We do not describe a club, a roster of residents, or a set of house rules. Those were not part of the published project. Lieve Maes is the project architect for housing and has been at the studio since 2014. The court is the studio's housing work, not a claim that one person designed it alone. Twenty-four apartments is the size of this court. It is not a minimum and not a maximum for the next brief.

01

Small apartment buildings

Linden Court is also the small apartment building on our list. Four storeys of timber-clad housing, deck access, and a garden, in Leuven, 2022, 24 apartments. We do not have a second named apartment building to put beside it, so this row stays with Linden Court and reads the building as apartments rather than as the shared court alone. The timber frame is the structure. Deck access is how you reach the homes. The garden is shared. A small building, for us, means a court of this kind: enough homes to need a common outdoor room, few enough that the access and the garden still belong to the people who live there.

We will not invent another town or another unit count to make the list look longer. Fees for housing use the practice list. A feasibility study is €3,800. Sketch design is from €9,500 and includes a model at 1:100. Full service is 9 % of the build cost. We do not promise a sales price or a completion date.

Title

Explanation

01 · Leuven · 2022

Linden Court, Leuven

Co-housing of 24 apartments with a shared garden, a timber frame and deck access, completed in 2022.

The shared yard between the blocks is where the project is read: benches, bicycles and a garden the residents keep.

pages.title: Renovation
pages.content:
03 · Work

Renovation

Renovation at Kosei Architects is the reuse of industrial buildings, told as a before and an after, not as a new object on a clear site.

00 Reuse of an industrial building

01 Old Mill studios, Ghent

00

Reuse of an industrial building

The published project is Old Mill studios in Ghent. Before the work, the building was a flour mill. After the work, completed in 2024, it holds 14 workshops across 1,600 m². The hall that remains is brick. New white steel is set against that older masonry, and daylight is brought into the workshops. We kept the job of the shell, which is to be a large room, and changed the use inside it.

The same habit shows up in Ostend, where Harbour Workshops kept the steel frame of a 1960s warehouse and added a timber mezzanine. The mill is the renovation we write up here. We do not claim that every industrial building can become workshops, and we do not say a structure is sound before the site visit. Brief and site visit takes 2 weeks. Feasibility, if you need a planning check and two massing options, is €3,800.

Old Mill studios, Ghent

A flour mill, kept in brick and white steel, now 14 workshops across 1,600 m².

01

Old Mill studios, Ghent

Old Mill studios is the one renovation row. Place: Ghent. Year: 2024. Type: renovation. Area: 1,600 m². Before: a flour mill. After: 14 workshops. The photograph of the project shows the brick mill hall, the white steel, and the daylight in the renovated room. We do not add a tenant list, a rent, or a change in floor area. 1,600 m² is the area we publish, not a before-and-after pair.

Fourteen is the number of workshops, not a density target. The project is also listed under Workplaces because the workshops are rooms where people work. On this page the point is the reuse. A first meeting about a building like this is free, 60 minutes at the studio or on site, with a written note of the brief. Sketch design, if the study goes on, starts from €9,500. Permit drawings start from €14,000. Full service is 9 % of the build cost. Construction runs per the contract. We do not promise a permit.

pages.title: Services
pages.content:
04 · Services

Services

Work is commissioned in stages, and each stage has a deliverable we can name.

00 Deliverables at each stage

01 The six services

02 Prices

00

Deliverables at each stage

Brief and site visit takes 2 weeks. You leave it with a written note of the brief, begun in a first meeting of 60 minutes at the studio or on site. Sketch design takes 6 to 8 weeks and delivers plans, sections, a model at 1:100, and a cost estimate. Permit drawings take 10 to 12 weeks and deliver the full permit set, with consultants coordinated, and the submission. The construction stage runs per the contract. Full service carries all of those stages and adds site meetings and a handover file.

Two further services sit beside the stages. A feasibility study delivers a site and planning check, two massing options, an area schedule, and a cost range. Interior workplace fit-out delivers a layout, finishes, and a furniture plan, priced per square metre. The six rows below are the services as we sell them. The four stages are how a full commission moves. We do not promise a permit, a build cost, or a date.

Title

Explanation

01 · Free · 60 min

First meeting

The first meeting lasts 60 minutes, at the studio on Quai des Charbonnages 12, 1080 Brussels, or on your site. It is by appointment.

The studio is open Monday to Friday, 09:00 to 18:00, and closed on Saturday and Sunday. The meeting is free. What you take away is a written note of the brief: the question the building has to answer, in plain language. It is not a design, not a set of plans, and not a cost estimate. Those belong to later lines. People use the hour to say whether they need a workplace, housing, or a renovation, and to ask how the later fees work. Anna Kosei or Rui Almeida may sit in, with whoever the stage needs. You do not need a finished programme before you come. You need the question, and access to the site if the meeting is held there. The brief and site visit stage that continues from this note takes 2 weeks.

↗

02 · 2 weeks

Feasibility study

A feasibility study costs €3,800, excluding VAT. It includes a site and planning check, two massing options, an area schedule, and a cost range.

The cost range is a range, not a tender and not a promised construction price. Two massing options means two ways the volume might sit on the site, studied enough to compare, not a finished architectural scheme. The area schedule sets down how much floor the options imply. We use this study when the question is still whether to build, convert, or stop. It is separate from the free first meeting and separate from sketch design. Harbour Workshops, Linden Court, Old Mill studios, and the Rivière school annex all passed through real sites. A new job starts with its own site, not with their areas copied forward. 4,200 m², 24 apartments, 1,600 m², and 900 m² belong to those four projects only. The fee for this study is fixed at €3,800. It is not marked from.

↗

03 · 6–8 weeks

Sketch design

Sketch design starts from €9,500, excluding VAT. The word from means a start, not a cap.

Included are plans, sections, a model at 1:100, and a cost estimate. The stage takes 6 to 8 weeks. The estimate is an estimate. It is not a builder's price and not a locked figure. The model at this stage is at 1:100. The timber model of Harbour Workshops that we photograph is a different scale, 1:50, and belongs to that project. Inès Laurent, model maker and visualisation since 2020, makes models in the studio. Sketch design is where the question from the brief becomes drawings you can review before a permit set is started. We draw slowly on purpose, so the building can be used for a long time. If the project is still only a hunch, stay with the feasibility study at €3,800 rather than opening this stage. Both can be discussed in the free first meeting.

↗

04 · 10–12 weeks

Permit drawings

Permit drawings start from €14,000, excluding VAT. From is a starting figure, not a ceiling.

Included are the full permit set, consultants coordinated, and the submission. The stage takes 10 to 12 weeks of our work. Clara Vogt leads technical design and permits and has been at the studio since 2017. Coordination of consultants means their drawings are brought into the set we submit. It does not mean we employ every trade under this fee, and it does not mean an authority will say yes. We do not promise a permit. Submission means we assemble the set and submit it. The weeks stated are our stage, not the authority's review, which has no number on this site. A workplace, a housing court, a mill conversion, and a school annex all need their own permit path. We will not describe a typical approval. If the project stops before this stage, you are not buying it inside the sketch fee.

↗

05 · All stages

Full service, design to handover

Full service runs from design to handover and costs 9 % of the build cost, excluding VAT. It includes all stages, site meetings, and a handover file.

The percentage is not a fixed euro sum. It moves with the build cost. We do not publish an example build cost, and we do not say in advance what the build cost will be. A cost range from feasibility and a cost estimate from sketch design are earlier readings, not this fee locked in. Yusuf Demir follows the site and the construction stage and has been at the studio since 2019. The construction stage itself is priced in time as per the contract, not as a count of weeks. Site meetings are part of full service. The handover file is the record you receive at the end. Stages inside the percentage still take the time already stated: 2 weeks, then 6 to 8, then 10 to 12, then construction per the contract. Hiring full service does not turn those spans into a fixed end date.

↗

06 · Per m²

Interior workplace fit-out

Interior workplace fit-out is €38 per m², excluding VAT. The fee covers layout, finishes, and a furniture plan.

It is the service for a floor that already has a shell, when the question is how people sit, what the surfaces are, and how furniture is set out. Harbour Workshops was more than a fit-out. It included a timber mezzanine, roof lights, and work to a warehouse frame, and it is an office of 4,200 m². We do not multiply 4,200 by €38 and call that the fee for Ostend. That sum is not a published figure, and the fit-out rate is not how that whole project was priced. Use €38 per m² for layout, finishes, and a furniture plan. Use sketch design, permit drawings, or full service when the work includes the building itself. The fit-out row is the sixth service. It does not include a model, a permit set, or site meetings unless those are hired on their own lines.

↗

02

Prices

All fees are in euro and exclude VAT. The full price list, with what each fee includes, is on the fees page.

See the fees↗

First meeting

A first meeting is free: 60 minutes at the studio or on site, and a written note of the brief.

pages.title: Process
pages.content:
05 · Studio

Process

The first stage is the brief and the site visit.

00 Brief and site visit2 weeks

01 Sketch design6–8 weeks

02 Permit drawings10–12 weeks

03 Construction stagePer contract

00

Brief and site visit

It takes 2 weeks. It starts from a question, not from a style. The free first meeting, 60 minutes at the studio or on site, produces a written note of the brief. The rest of the two weeks is the visit and the work of writing that question down clearly enough to draw from. We look at what is already there. At Harbour Workshops that was a 1960s warehouse with a steel frame.

At Old Mill studios it was a flour mill. At Linden Court and at the Rivière school annex the sites were the places those buildings now stand. You do not leave this stage with plans, a model, or a permit set. You leave with the note, and with a shared account of the site. If a cost range and two massing options are needed before any sketch, that is the feasibility study, a separate service at €3,800, not an automatic part of these two weeks.

01

Sketch design

Sketch design takes 6 to 8 weeks. The deliverables are plans, sections, a model at 1:100, and a cost estimate. The fee starts from €9,500, excluding VAT. This is the stage where the brief becomes a building you can look at, still slowly. The sentence we work under is simple: we draw slowly so buildings can be used for a long time. The model is physical. The timber model of Harbour Workshops at 1:50 is the study model of that office, a three-storey building on the studio table.

The model included in this stage, for a commission, is at 1:100. Both are models. They are not the same scale. The cost estimate is a design-stage estimate. It is not a contract sum and not a locked price. Rui Almeida, partner and architect since 2011, reviews this stage with Anna Kosei. Eight people work at one table, so the sketch is seen by the person who will later draw the permit set and by the person who makes the model.

On site

The brief from week one still has to answer once the frame is standing.

02

Permit drawings

Permit drawings take 10 to 12 weeks. The deliverables are the full permit set, consultants coordinated, and the submission. The fee starts from €14,000, excluding VAT. Clara Vogt, technical design and permits since 2017, holds this stage. Coordination means the consultants' work is brought into one set. It does not mean a permit will be granted. We submit the drawings.

The authority's time is not part of the 10 to 12 weeks, and we do not publish a review period. No project on this site is offered as proof that a permit is easy. Harbour Workshops, Linden Court, Old Mill studios, and the Rivière school annex are finished buildings. Their years, 2023, 2022, 2024, and 2021, are completion or in-use years, not permit-decision dates. We will not back-calculate how long each authority took. If your project needs this stage, it is priced on its own or inside full service at 9 % of the build cost.

03

Construction stage

The construction stage runs per the contract. There is no week count for it on this site. Full service includes the stage, the site meetings, and a handover file, and the fee for full service is 9 % of the build cost. Yusuf Demir follows site and construction and has been at the studio since 2019. A site meeting is a meeting on the building while it is being built. It is not the opening site visit of the brief stage. One journal note shows an architect and a client in hard hats on a timber-frame site. That is this stage.

Linden Court and the Rivière school annex are timber buildings. Harbour Workshops put a timber mezzanine into a steel frame. The mill renovation set white steel against old brick. What we watch depends on the contract. The school annex was built in 11 months. That number is the construction of that annex, not this stage's standard length. We do not promise a handover date. The handover file records what was built.

04

What the client supplies

You supply the question, and you supply access. The question is the use: 180 desks, or 24 apartments, or workshops in a mill, or classrooms for a school. Those numbers are examples from finished work, not a form you must fill with the same digits. Access means we can walk the site during the brief stage, and that we can hold the first meeting there if that is the better room. If existing drawings exist, we ask to see them. If they do not, the visit is the start. You also supply decisions when each stage is reviewed: after the sketch, after the permit set, and during construction under the contract.

You do not supply a fixed build cost. Where full service is hired, the fee is 9 % of the build cost once that cost exists. You do not supply a permit. We prepare and submit the set. The authority decides. Mei Tan, studio manager since 2018, arranges the appointment. The meeting itself is free and lasts 60 minutes.

08 · Studio

About

Kosei Architects was founded in 2008.

00 Founding

01 Method

02 Values

03 Anna Kosei

00

Founding

The founder is Anna Kosei, an architect, at the studio since that year. The studio is at Quai des Charbonnages 12, 1080 Brussels, Belgium. Eight people work here. The door is open Monday to Friday, 09:00 to 18:00, and closed on Saturday and Sunday. A first meeting is by appointment. We did not grow by collecting offices in other cities. The published buildings are elsewhere, because that is where the sites were: Ostend, Leuven, Ghent, and Namur.

The practice stayed in Brussels. Founding, for us, is that year, that address, and that table. We do not tell a longer origin story. There is no prize list and no press list. The early work of the studio is the method you can still see: a question, a model, then a building people use. Rui Almeida joined as partner and architect in 2011. The other six people came in the years printed on the studio page, from 2014 through 2020.

01

Method

The method has four stages. Brief and site visit, 2 weeks. Sketch design, 6 to 8 weeks, with plans, sections, a model at 1:100, and a cost estimate. Permit drawings, 10 to 12 weeks, with the full permit set, consultants coordinated, and submission. Construction, per the contract, with site meetings and a handover file when full service is hired. Full service is 9 % of the build cost. We draw slowly so buildings can be used for a long time. Every project starts with a question, not a style.

The line we put on the first page is the method in one breath: from a model on the table to buildings in use. The model of Harbour Workshops, at 1:50, is the clearest picture of that. A logistics firm needed 180 desks. The model sat on the table. The warehouse kept its steel frame. The floor has been in use since 2023. The same order applies to housing and to renovation. We do not skip the question because a site is attractive.

02

Values

We can point to a few values because the work already shows them. We would rather start from the question than from a style. We would rather draw slowly if that helps a building stay in use. We would rather say the fee before we draw a line, which is why the price list is public, in euro, excluding VAT, with no hidden fourth column. We would rather keep a sound structure when the brief allows it. At Harbour Workshops the steel frame of the 1960s warehouse stayed. At Old Mill studios a flour mill became 14 workshops instead of being wiped clear.

We would rather show a model than talk in adjectives. We do not hold these up as a certificate. We do not promise a permit, a build cost, a completion date, or a copy of an older result. Daylight at every desk in Ostend is a result from that office. It is not a moral claim about every room we will ever draw. Eight people, one table, is a working arrangement, not a slogan we need to stretch.

03

Anna Kosei

Anna Kosei founded Kosei Architects in 2008 and still works as an architect in the studio. The portrait on this page shows her by a window in the studio, holding a piece of a model. That is the public picture: a person at the table, not a biography of schools and earlier firms. She has been here since 2008. The partner beside her in the practice is Rui Almeida, here since 2011. The other people are Lieve Maes, Samuel Okafor, Clara Vogt, Yusuf Demir, Inès Laurent, and Mei Tan. Their roles and years are on the studio page.

Anna's part of the method is the part the studio still repeats. Start with the question. Put a model on the table. Draw so the building can be used for a long time. Take the first meeting yourself when that is what the brief needs. The meeting is 60 minutes, free, at Quai des Charbonnages 12 or on the site, and it produces a written note. Phone the studio on +32 2 555 01 84 during open hours.

posts.title: The model on the table
posts.excerpt: Harbour Workshops was a timber model at 1:50 on our Brussels table before it was a floor of 180 desks in an Ostend warehouse.
posts.content:
Before Harbour Workshops was a floor of desks in Ostend, it was a timber model at 1:50 on a pale table in Brussels. The model shows a three-storey office building in light timber. It sits at eye level against a white wall, with tracing paper and a steel ruler at the edge of the table. We keep that photograph because it is the honest start of the project. The building people use now came after the model, not the other way round.

The question in front of the model was specific. A logistics firm needed one floor for 180 desks in a 1960s warehouse. The published area is 4,200 m². Nobody asked the studio for a style. They asked whether that warehouse could hold a working floor. Kosei Architects was founded in 2008 and works from Quai des Charbonnages 12, 1080 Brussels. Eight people share one table. The model of this office was made there. Inès Laurent, model maker and visualisation, has been at the studio since 2020 and cuts timber for the models we use. We do not pin this model on one pair of hands. It is studio work, the same as the drawings.

A model at the start of a job is not a miniature of a decision already taken. It is how we look. You can walk around it, see where a floor lands, and see where light has to come from, while the building is still timber strips and glue. Sketch design, as a commissioned stage, includes a model at 1:100, together with plans, sections, and a cost estimate. That stage takes 6 to 8 weeks and the fee starts from €9,500, excluding VAT. The Harbour model we show in the studio is at 1:50. The two scales do different jobs. One to one hundred belongs to the sketch-design service. One to fifty is the study model of this particular office. Putting both numbers in the same sentence without saying that would blur the fee and the photograph.

What the model was testing, the building then did. The work was a timber mezzanine and roof lights, and the steel frame of the warehouse was kept. New timber went into an existing structure. The frame was not the obstacle. It was the part worth holding onto. We draw slowly so a building can be used for a long time, and keeping a sound frame is part of that. The same instinct shows in Ghent, where Old Mill studios took a flour mill and turned it into 14 workshops across 1,600 m², completed in 2024, with brick, white steel, and daylight. Reuse is not a slogan we add after the fact. It is what those two briefs allowed.

Harbour Workshops has been in use since 2023. There are 180 desks, and daylight reaches every desk. That sentence is the result of this project. It is not a standard we paste onto the next office. The Rivière school annex in Namur, a timber building of 6 classrooms and 900 m², was built in 11 months and completed in 2021. Linden Court in Leuven, co-housing of 24 apartments with a shared garden, a timber frame, and deck access, was completed in 2022. Those are other buildings, with other questions. The model habit is what they share with Ostend. Each one was studied before it was a room someone had to use every day.

The path from table to site is the same four stages on every full commission. Brief and site visit takes 2 weeks. Sketch design takes 6 to 8 weeks. Permit drawings take 10 to 12 weeks and include the full permit set, consultants coordinated, and the submission, from €14,000. The construction stage runs per the contract. Full service, design to handover, covers all of those stages plus site meetings and a handover file, and the fee is 9 % of the build cost. The percentage moves with the build cost. We do not state what that cost will be, and we do not promise a permit or a completion date. A feasibility study, if the question is still whether to build, is €3,800 and includes a site and planning check, two massing options, an area schedule, and a cost range.

If you want to see the model, the studio is open Monday to Friday, 09:00 to 18:00, and closed on Saturday and Sunday. The entrance is a glass door in a white brick facade. A first meeting is free, lasts 60 minutes, and can be at the studio or on your site. You leave with a written note of the brief. Phone +32 2 555 01 84 or write during open hours. Bring the question. The model comes after that, not before.

posts.title: Cutting the 1:50 model
posts.excerpt: Inès Laurent at the bench, timber strips, and why the Harbour Workshops model was built before the mezzanine was drawn.
posts.content:
The 1:50 timber model for Harbour Workshops was built before the mezzanine was drawn. Inès Laurent cut the strips at her bench, one floor at a time, and the studio looked at the model on the table before it looked at any section.

A model shows a thing a drawing hides: where daylight lands on a desk, and where a stair takes too much floor. We keep the model on the table until the building is in use.

posts.title: A site morning in hard hats
posts.excerpt: What the architect and the client look at together once a timber frame is standing, and what the brief from week one still has to answer.
posts.content:
Once a timber frame is standing, the architect and the client walk it together. The first question is always the same: does the room do what the brief from week one asked of it?

Yusuf Demir follows the site through the construction stage and keeps the drawings aligned with the work. Site meetings are part of full service, which is 9 percent of build cost, excl. VAT.

posts.title: The joint, up close
posts.excerpt: A timber beam, a steel connector and the raking light on a detail that has to stay precise from the model to the building.
posts.content:
A timber beam, a steel connector and the raking light across them. This is a detail that has to stay precise from the 1:50 model to the building on site.

Clara Vogt prepares the permit drawings where such joints are fixed. Permit drawings take ten to twelve weeks and start from €14,000, excl. VAT.
